agents.role: Runs the accountability board and the PAR timer. Raises par-check-due, air-low-estimate, crew-unaccounted, and mayday alerts. Advises the incident commander; it never orders a crew.
Keeps the incident timeline as it happens and seals it at all-clear, so the record of the incident is complete and checkable afterward.
Keeps apparatus and crew roster state current across the incident: committed, available, out of service.
The only agent in this pack that may post across worlds. Sends summary counts (never names) to hospital and EMS worlds when casualties are expected, and receives capacity and scene-safety summaries.

alerts.carries: The crew id and the PAR due time. Stays on the fireground; the accountability officer acts on it.
The crew id and the estimated minutes of air remaining, marked as an estimate, never a measurement.
The crew id and last known location inside the structure. Local only; names of members never ride any bus line.
A summary only: incident id, that a mayday is declared, and casualty counts by severity. No member names, no patient names.

receives.carries: Emergency department capacity state and diversion status as counts and states, never patient information.
Road closures and scene perimeter state affecting apparatus access, summarized; no police record details.
How many transport units are committed and their destination hospitals, as counts.

sends.carries: Incident id, casualty counts by severity (critical, serious, minor), and an arrival window estimate. Counts only.
Incident id, casualty counts by severity, and the staging location for transport units. Counts only.

firstboot.label: Unit roster: apparatus and the members riding each unit
Chief or admin contact for this installation

bus_summary: Casualty counts by severity on a mayday or multi-casualty incident
Unit availability counts for mutual-aid coordination
Incident id and incident type for cross-world summaries
local_only: Member names and assignments on the accountability board
Interior positions and last known locations
Full incident timeline before it is sealed and reviewed

parts.proven: Pinning tests on fixtures (tests/test_fdny_par_clock.py). UNPROVEN, stated plainly: not yet run on a booted Meta OS image, in a real station exercise, or wired as a systemd unit.
parts.what: The PAR clock: per-crew interval countdown, par-check-due (warning) and crew-unaccounted (critical, life-safety) alerts in the FND-020 frozen line format, enter/exit/complete commands for the human accountability officer, timeline and dedupe state on disk, pure core plus CLI, no model calls, no bus posts, no sensors.

summary: Fireground accountability and incident record pack: tracks who is inside a structure, elapsed time and air estimates, PAR check timing, apparatus and crew roster state, and the sealed incident timeline. PARTIAL: the PAR clock runtime (worlds/fdny/runtime/par_clock.py) exists and is pinning-tested; every other declared watcher remains definition only, and nothing here runs a real fire department system.
summary_note: Accountability aid only: it advises and records. It never orders crews, never dispatches, never guesses where a crew is, and never completes a PAR on its own. Command decisions stay with the incident commander.

urgency.meaning: Mayday and crew-unaccounted events. Preempts everything else on the bus.
PAR checks due and air estimates running low.
Roster and unit state changes during an incident.
Sealed incident timeline and end-of-incident summary.

inputs: entry and exit reports from the accountability officer
watchers.watches: Crew accountability on the fireground: which members are inside the structure, their entry time, elapsed interior time, and estimated remaining air, against the incident clock.
PAR (personnel accountability report) check timing: when the next PAR check falls due for each interior crew and whether it completed.
Apparatus and crew roster state: which units are on scene, committed, available, or out of service, and who is riding each unit.
The incident timeline: dispatch, arrival, entry, PAR results, mayday events, and all-clear, kept as the verified record of the incident.
